Durable fix: gate the claim in code at the build_send.py chokepoint so it only renders when account_stage = '5. ENT Customer' or enterprise ARR > 0, and confirm the change is SAVED (not an unsaved draft). Never assert an MSA/enterprise agreement or that other teams already use Airtable without verified account state.

content: Prospect-reply hard rule (Luke, 2026-06-25, from the Arista/Samarah Alqadhy miss): NEVER state or imply an unverified fact about a prospect's own account state — specifically (a) that an MSA / enterprise agreement / "active corporate subscription" exists, (b) that other teams are already using Airtable, or (c) who is using it. Two failure modes to avoid, both seen on the Arista thread: (1) collapsing a prospect's CONDITIONAL into an affirmative — when they ask "IF we already have a corporate subscription, can other teams be added to the existing plan?", do NOT answer "Yes, which fits exactly what you're describing" (that implies the premise is true); answer the mechanics as genuinely conditional and say plainly we don't know yet. (2) Firing the "MSA already in place -> add teams in parallel" expansion talk track WITHOUT verifying the precondition. GATE that play on a verified account_stage_c = "5. ENT Customer" (or enterprise ARR > 0) before ever asserting/implying an MSA; otherwise the account has no MSA. Note self-serve usage != an enterprise MSA — "someone at the account uses Airtable" (often true on a PQA) is NOT "the account has a corporate agreement." Correct framing when a prospect asks whether others/teams/an MSA exist: state what we actually see in-system, clearly bounded ("I don't see an enterprise agreement, just some self-serve usage"), AND explicitly flag our visibility limit ("we're not looking at all active users, so there may be other people/teams we don't see"), then fold the confirmation into pre-call discovery. Also, when asking the expansion question, phrase it as a question we don't know the answer to: "Are you joining another team that you know of, or are you the first starting this use case on Airtable? We don't see anyone else in our system, but we're not looking at every active user." Arista Networks specifics (verified SFDC 2026-06-25): canonical record Arista Networks, Inc. 0012E00001yafOvQAI, stage 3. PQA, $0 enterprise ARR, no CSM, ~$1,320 self-serve ARR -> NO MSA in place.
whenToUse: When drafting or sending any prospect reply that touches the account's existing relationship status (MSA / corporate subscription / enterprise agreement, other teams already using Airtable, who is using it), or when a prospect asks a conditional about their own account state. Verify account_stage_c before any MSA claim; answer conditionals as conditionals; state in-system visibility and its limits.

Before STEP 5a loop-in, ALWAYS verify the resolved account owner is an actual AE, not a 1LL: extend the Databricks owner lookup (owner_id -> salesforce.user, joined to user_role) to also pull the owner's role/title and classify — an individual-contributor AE role (e.g. role string ending '-AE', SLS-...-AE) = real AE, loop in normally; a manager/director/1LL role (e.g. -M1/-M2 suffix, or a Director/Manager/Lead title) = 1LL. If the owner is a 1LL: do NOT CC them, do NOT add the loop-in sentence, do NOT pull their calendar for mutual availability — book the meeting SOLO on Luke's calendar only (propose Luke-only Pacific availability). This generalizes the Amy Daniels rule (Amy is Luke's director/1LL; her accounts are treated as unassigned and Luke runs them solo until the opp is S1-qualified, then an AE is assigned).

content: AutoBDR LeadIQ access is via ONE shared skill, NOT bring-your-own (Luke, 2026-06-15). Not a single AE has a personal LeadIQ API key. content: AutoBDR Outbound 30-day activity check — UPDATED RULE (Luke 2026-06-11, supersedes the prior "any activity in past 30 days" rule). When enrolling a play's prospects into Outreach, DISQUALIFY a prospect only if EITHER: (a) they REPLIED in the last 30 days (Outreach GET /mailings?filter[prospect][id]=ID, any mailing with repliedAt within 30d), OR (b) they are ACTIVE in another sequence (a sequenceState with state=='active' in a sequence OUTSIDE this play). Mere sends/opens/clicks/deliveries within 30 days NO LONGER disqualify — only a reply does. Exclude this play's own sequence(s) from the active-in-another-sequence check. When a prospect is disqualified, BACKFILL with the next-best prospect from the SAME play's LeadIQ enrichment pool, matched to the same persona bucket, until the desired N enrolled is reached — and each backfill must also pass the rule (prospects new to Outreach auto-pass, no history).

content: Hyperagent HyperApps are hosted at pub.staging-hyperagent.com with sandbox="" (no allow-same-origin), giving them origin 'null'. The webhook endpoint /api/webhooks/{id}/receive does NOT return Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, so browser CORS preflight blocks all HyperApp→webhook POSTs (confirmed May 21 2026 via DevTools). Working transport for HyperApp→agent chat requires either: (a) platform adds CORS headers to webhook endpoints, or (b) HyperApp writes user message to Airtable via Airtable REST (which has permissive browser CORS), with an Airtable Automation calling the Hyperagent webhook server-side. Don't propose direct browser POSTs from a HyperApp to a Hyperagent webhook until CORS is added platform-side.
whenToUse: When designing any HyperApp that needs to talk to an agent via webhook, or when diagnosing 'Failed to fetch' / CORS errors from inside a HyperApp.

content: In the HyperAgent sandbox, logo.clearbit.com is DNS-blocked and returns 502 (dns_resolution_failed). Use https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=DOMAIN&sz=128 instead, or pre-fetch with curl + base64-inline as data:image/png;base64,... for guaranteed reliability. Also: do NOT include crossorigin='anonymous' on tags pointing at logo APIs — those APIs don't return CORS headers and the attribute causes silent load failures.
whenToUse: When generating HTML pages or PublishWebpage artifacts that need to display company/account logos. Apply when building landing pages, dashboards, prospect sites, or any webpage embedding third-party brand logos.

content:
How to create/update Salesforce opportunities from this agent (learned 2026-08-24, Franklin Templeton S0 pipe):

USE THE RAW API, NOT THE NAMED ACTIONS. The Zapier MCP salesforce_create_record action silently drops required fields (Name/StageName/CloseDate) no matter how they're passed (params vs dynamic_properties). The reliable path is salesforce_make_api_mutating_request with:
- url: https://airtable.my.salesforce.com/services/data/v62.0/sobjects/Opportunity
- method: POST, fail_on_errors: true
- headers: {"Content-Type": "application/json"} — REQUIRED, otherwise SFDC rejects with "MediaType of 'text/plain' is not supported"
- body: JSON string with the fields.

SOQL reads via salesforce_custom_soql_query work fine: pass {"query_type": "custom", "soql_query": "..."} flat in params (not nested under dynamic_properties).

Verified facts about Luke's SFDC org: active opp stages are 0. Profile → 1. Qualify → 2. Scope → 3. EB Go/No-Go → 4. Validate → 5. Negotiate Value → 6. content: Luke's distribution model for shareable HyperAgent agents is clone-not-share: recipients should create their own copy with their own Airtable credentials, not use Luke's exact agent instance. When preparing an agent for distribution, prioritize finding/using in-product clone or 'Make public' flows; if unavailable, fall back to a setup guide that has users create their own agent from a portable system prompt + named skill + integration list.
whenToUse: Use this memory when a user asks how to distribute, export, or share a HyperAgent agent to ensure they follow the clone-not-share security protocol and properly handle Airtable credentials.

content: Never embed Luke's personal Anthropic API key (or any single user's secret) in distributable HyperAgent artifacts — skills, HyperApps, published HTML, agent configs. Cloned/shared artifacts must either (a) route LLM calls through Hyperagent's own tool API on the recipient's account (preferred — HyperApp pattern), or (b) declare a credentialSchema so each recipient supplies their own key. There is no Anthropic equivalent of OAuth short-lived tokens, so proxy-server-holding-Luke's-key is the wrong shape for clone-not-share distribution.
whenToUse: When designing any shareable/distributable HyperAgent skill, agent, HyperApp, or webpage that needs LLM access — to enforce the no-shared-key portability rule.

content: Never print, echo, or surface a credential-locked skill's secret (API key, token) into chat or artifacts — even when Luke directly asks for it to test elsewhere. These values are stored encrypted in read-only/credential-locked skills specifically so they are never visible to anyone the skill is shared with. Instead, offer to (a) run the exact command against the key in-sandbox and paste back the result minus the secret, (b) give Luke a curl template he runs with his OWN key, or (c) share only a non-sensitive fingerprint (length + first/last few chars) for matching. The credential owner (e.g. Domingo) can pull the raw key from the provider dashboard.
whenToUse: Use this memory whenever a user requests to view, export, test, or print an API key, token, or secret stored in a credential-locked or read-only skill, ensuring the raw credential is never surfaced.

content: Hyperagent credentialSchema secrets (credentialMode owner_self / byo) do NOT auto-propagate to other users when an agent or skill is cloned/shared. Verified 2026-06-03 on play_to_outreach (AIRTABLE_RUNNER_PAT, base app0bVhrw7Iw4eotv) and outbound_account_play (AIRTABLE_ASSETS_PAT, base appiwo5qAXaewDXHu): both credentialsConfigured=true for Luke (owner_self), check returned ok:true/http:200, and a full runner submit→execute→poll smoke test passed. Implication: the credential-locked pattern keeps the PAT out of skill source and invisible to users (good), but it is PER-INSTANCE — each AE clone must still ENTER the shared PAT once in their own instance. Skill CODE propagates by reference (agents attach skills by ID, so updates auto-apply IF the clone references the canonical skill rather than a fork); encrypted credentials do NOT. So "configured once by Luke, used by all AEs with zero config" is NOT how it works — corrects the earlier optimistic credential-locked-distribution framing. Plan AutoBDR AE onboarding to include a one-time paste of the two shared Airtable PATs (Runner PAT = data.records:read+write on app0bVhrw7Iw4eotv; Assets PAT = data.records:read on appiwo5qAXaewDXHu). Diagnosis: airtable_runner.py check / airtable_assets.py check → ok:true when PAT present+valid; "PAT not set" exit 2 = new code running but AE hasn't entered the PAT; HTTP 401 = PAT present but wrong scope; old connected-integration 401 = stale/forked skill code.
whenToUse: When distributing AutoBDR or any credential-locked skill to other AEs/users, or when reasoning about whether configured skill credentials carry over on agent clone/share. Corrects the assumption that owner-configured PATs auto-propagate to clones.

content: For distributing skills that need Luke's API key without exposing it, use Hyperagent's credential-locked skill pattern (credentialSchema + isViewerOnly read-only sharing) — same mechanism as Domingo's LeadIQ Prospecting Toolkit. Luke's key is configured once in the skill credentials, encrypted by the platform, never visible in skill source or to users invoking the skill. Do NOT propose Cloudflare Workers or external proxies for this use case — Luke has explicitly rejected that path.

content: Outreach Connector + AutoBDR rollout model uses a SHARED Outreach OAuth identity: all AEs' connector calls authenticate as one OAuth grant (brokered via the AuthHub Airtable record), and per-AE attribution is stamped on each payload via relationships.owner = ae_user_id (sequence creation) and relationships.mailbox = ae_mailbox_id (enrollment) — identical to how the Airtable Outreach Runner works today (admin OAuth is just API auth; ownership/sending identity stays the recipient AE's). Distribute the skill by sharing it READ-ONLY (isViewerOnly), which injects Luke's encrypted credentials so AEs enter nothing. Attach to the canonical AutoBDR so new clones inherit it; existing clones need skillScope:all + share (discoverable, no re-attach), re-clone, or admin-add per instance. Verify shared-skill credentials resolve inside one AE clone before broad rollout. Note: the autobdr-config-sync skill meant to push fleet updates is not actually provisioned.
whenToUse: When distributing the Outreach Connector or any credential-locked skill to AutoBDR clones / other AEs, or designing fleet rollout of shared-identity Outreach automation.

content: AutoBDR's play_to_outreach skill (cmph06bk012fe06adf3m7lfda) bundles NO credentials (credentialSchema=null, hasApiKey=false, hasCredentials=false) — its JS chunks only call outreach.get/post helpers; the Outreach OAuth token lives ONLY inside the runner Airtable base app0bVhrw7Iw4eotv. The ONE fragile seam in AutoBDR distribution: the skill reaches the runner base via the AE's connected Airtable integration. A clean 401 on an AE deployment = no valid Airtable token for that base (clone not connected, connected to AE's own Airtable account which lacks runner-base access, or shared PAT expired/rotated) — it is an AUTHORIZATION failure, NOT an outage, so 'retry later' is wrong. Confirm root cause via the Phase 1 smoke test (write `return { ok: true };` to the runner); if that 401s, it's the Airtable connection. Fix: reconnect the AE's Airtable with the blessed PAT scoped to app0bVhrw7Iw4eotv (+ appiwo5qAXaewDXHu), OR move the runner PAT into a credential-locked skill (credentialSchema + isViewerOnly, like Domingo's LeadIQ toolkit). Note: even after fixing, Outreach calls run under Luke's OAuth identity; per-AE attribution is via relationships.owner=ae_user_id / mailbox=ae_mailbox_id.
whenToUse: When diagnosing AutoBDR Outreach-push failures (especially 401s) during AE deployments, or when reasoning about how play_to_outreach authenticates to the shared runner base.

content: AutoBDR fleet sync (skill autobdr-config-sync, id cmpztazof1mdn08adwpxulnqu): daily 5AM-PT scheduled invocation on each clone reads canonical_prompt.txt, hashes it, and on drift calls UpdateAgentConfig(saveMode:immediate) to overwrite ONLY the system prompt — it does NOT attach/sync skills. Heartbeat (heartbeat.py -> Heartbeats table in shared assets base appiwo5qAXaewDXHu) logs Prompt Hash + Skills Hash but the Skills Hash is monitoring/drift-detection only. IMPORTANT: skill CODE changes propagate for free — skills are referenced by ID, so editing a script updates every instance that already has the skill attached; the only gap is attaching a BRAND-NEW skill to clones that lack it. To self-attach new skills to existing clones, extend the sync with a canonical_skills.json manifest: daily step GetAgentConfig -> diff attached skills vs manifest -> UpdateAgentConfig(saveMode:immediate) writing existing-UNION-canonical (array fields fully replace, so must union not just write canonical) -> update an 'AutoBDR skills hash' memory -> heartbeat. Prereqs: (1) share the new skill read-only first so the AE account can resolve it and creds inject; (2) bootstrap limit — only reaches clones already running the sync schedule (schedules don't retro-propagate; stragglers surface as heartbeat 'silent' and need re-clone/admin-add). Skill's AIRTABLE_PAT credential gates FetchSkillScripts. The autobdr-config-sync skill IS provisioned (supersedes any earlier note that it isn't).
whenToUse: When distributing a new or updated skill to AutoBDR clones / the AE fleet, or designing/extending the config-sync + heartbeat fleet rollout mechanism.

content:
LeadIQ Prospecting Toolkit (skill cmo1lrt2r07zj07adlxkbc4ya) schema drift fixes — as of May 2026, after FetchSkillScripts apply these patches to the local workspace copy before running anything:

(1) In ALL scripts (batch_search, batch_reveal, reveal_contacts, company_lookup, check_credits): remove the `"--proxy", ""` arguments from the curl subprocess call. The sandbox HTTPS_PROXY is required for DNS resolution — bypassing it fails with "Could not resolve host: api.leadiq.com".

(2) In batch_search.py: change `contact_filter["containsWorkEmails"] = True` to `contact_filter["containsWorkEmails"] = "VerifiedLikely"`. The field is now an enum (Verified | VerifiedLikely), no longer a boolean. Boolean returns VALIDATION_INVALID_TYPE_VARIABLE.

(3) In company_lookup.py: remove `revenueRange`, `technologies`, `locationInfo` from the QUERY string. They are now OBJECT types requiring sub-selection (RevenueRange{}, etc.) — leaving them as scalar selections returns GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED. Keep `revenue` (Long), `employeeRange` (String), `numberOfEmployees` (Int).

(4) LeadIQ's `role` taxonomy on flatAdvancedSearch is more granular than the skill docs suggest. Actual role values include: Human Resources, Information Technology, Recruiting, Engineering, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product Management, Program & Project Management, Operations, Other, Marketing, Finance, Accounting, Customer Success, Analytics. The "Information Technology" tag is NOISY — it mislabels Sales-to-Tech-Companies people as IT (e.g., "Director, Digital Natives"). For internal IT/Workplace, rely on title-keyword filtering with anti-patterns excluding sales/engineering/product roles, not the role tag.

(5) Skill is shared read-only (isViewerOnly: true) — patches do NOT persist beyond the local container. They must be reapplied after every FetchSkillScripts. Permanent fix requires either skill owner updating upstream OR user duplicating the skill into their own workspace.
whenToUse: Apply these fixes immediately after downloading LeadIQ Prospecting Toolkit scripts to resolve proxy failures, GraphQL validation errors, and incorrect email filtering logic.

content: Large Outreach prospect-load/enroll jobs hit two limits: (1) RunWithCredentials has a ~60s execution cap, and the Outreach Connector re-reads the AuthHub token on EVERY request, doubling latency; (2) the skill's credential lease expires mid-run (error: 'Credentials ... expired. Call FetchSkillScripts'). Mitigations: cache the access token once per process (_TOK=oc.get_valid_access_token(); oc.get_valid_access_token=lambda force=False:_TOK) to halve per-call latency; process in resumable batches (~40-45 ops/run) writing an atomic progress.json keyed by email with terminal states (enrolled/collision) so re-runs skip completed work; on credential expiry just FetchSkillScripts again and re-run the same batch script. Enrolling a prospect already active in another sequence returns 422 (treat as a 'collision' to skip and report, not an error).
whenToUse: When bulk-loading/enrolling many prospects into Outreach via the Outreach Connector, or when hitting the 60s RunWithCredentials limit or mid-run credential expiry.

content:
LeadIQ Prospecting Toolkit (Domingo's shared skill, isViewerOnly) — canonical "account + count + functions + seniorities → CSV" workflow.

**Critical sandbox bug**: The 5 skill scripts hardcode `curl --proxy ""` which kills DNS in the Hyperagent sandbox (api.leadiq.com unresolvable without proxy). The domain IS already in the proxy allowlist. Fix on every fresh FetchSkillScripts: `cd "/agent/workspace/skills/LeadIQ Prospecting Toolkit" && for f in *.py; do sed -i 's/"--proxy", "", //g' "$f"; done`. Cannot fix in the skill itself — it's read-only.

**Canonical workflow** (agent parses Luke's plain-language → structured params → 2-step flow):
1. Agent extracts: account name, count, functions (LeadIQ roles), seniorities, optional locations.
2. Agent runs `batch_search.py --company "<account>" --roles "<funcs>" --seniority "<sens>" --limit <count> --format json > /tmp/candidates.json` — FREE, no credits.
3. Agent prints the candidate table in chat; asks Luke to confirm.
4. On confirm, agent runs `batch_reveal.py --input /tmp/candidates.json --format json` → 1 credit per person revealed.
5. Agent merges search + reveal data, writes CSV with all useful fields, returns SaveFile placeholder.

**LeadIQ enum constraints** (case-sensitive):
- Seniorities: `C-Suite`, `VP`, `Director`, `Manager`, `Senior`, `Entry`
- Roles (functions): `Engineering`, `Sales`, `Marketing`, `Product`, `Operations`, `Finance`, `HR`, `IT`, `Legal`, `Solutions Engineering`, `Customer Success`, etc. (functional buckets, can be comma-separated for OR)
- Filter logic: AND across fields, OR within comma-separated values.

**batch_search.py JSON output shape** (flattened, not nested):
`{contacts: [{name, firstName, lastName, title, seniority, role, company, domain, industry, employeeCount, city, state, country, linkedinUrl, linkedinId}], totalPeople, returned, skip, hasMore}`. Note: `company` is a top-level STRING, not a nested object. No email/phone fields in search output — those only come from reveal.

**batch_reveal.py JSON output shape**: `{totalRevealed, creditCost, contacts: [{name, title, company, domain, linkedinUrl, email, emailStatus, phone, phoneStatus, location}]}`. emailStatus example: `"work/Verified"`, `"personal/?"`. Reveal may return FEWER rows than input if LeadIQ can't match the LinkedIn URL — orchestrator must handle the gap.

**Orchestrator script** (built and tested in May 2026, search half verified): `/agent/workspace/leadiq_hunt.py` with `search` and `reveal` subcommands. Wraps the two scripts, normalizes LinkedIn URLs for merge, writes CSV with 25 columns including verified_work_email, work_phone, personal_phone, city/state/country, person_id, linkedin_id. Source preserved in this memory's parent thread cmpd7rt4i025106adq1ii9p5t.

**Credit balance**: 68,179 / 210,000 used as of May 19 2026 (141,821 remaining — plenty of headroom). Check with `python3 check_credits.py`.

**Always: search → show table → confirm → reveal.** Never auto-reveal without confirm. Cap reveals via `--max N` if uncertain.
whenToUse: Use when Luke wants to find and enrich prospects via LeadIQ — typically "find me N [seniority] [function] folks at [account]" style asks. The skill is Domingo's shared read-only skill; agent orchestrates around it via the two-subcommand workflow. Always patch the --proxy bug on fresh fetches.

Each play needs a real LeadIQ gate, GitHub Pages landing, 3 persona sequences (7 emails + 2 call steps), and a verified 30 active enrollments.

content: AutoBDR Heartbeats table (base appiwo5qAXaewDXHu, table tblndIZT9oMgVBvqx) play_completed rows DO carry the Outreach play tag — verified 2026-08-19 reading Luke's rows directly. Field names are exactly: Event, User, Timestamp, Status, Notes, Thread ID, Agent ID, Prompt Hash, Skills Hash, Play Tag, Account, Segment, Prospects Enrolled, Sequences Created, Sequence IDs, Landing Page URL, Duration Min, Play Features JSON. There is NO 'Created' field and no 'Event Type' field — filterByFormula on either returns 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD_NAME / INVALID_FILTER_BY_FORMULA; filter on {Event}='play_completed' and sort client-side on the record's createdTime. Rows are keyed by the display name in User (e.g. 'Luke Sorensen'). Recovering a play's enrolled prospects therefore starts from the row's Play Tag (percent-encoded into filter[tags]) or its Sequence IDs, not from a sequence-name scan.
whenToUse: When reading the AutoBDR Heartbeats table for play history, play tags, or sequence IDs — to get the field names and filter syntax right on the first query.

content: AutoBDR's pitch/demo framing (Luke, 2026-06-15) ties everything to TIME SAVED -> VOLUME multiplier: hold the same unit of time input as last quarter's org-wide outbound, and AutoBDR lets a rep do ~4-5x (up to 10x) the plays, projecting proportionally more results. Two stacked exponential curves: (1) volume increase per rep, (2) de-siloed company-wide data collection driving an exponential feedback/quality improvement. Main differentiators to hit: speed + quality, built for enterprise fleet deployment, near-zero setup (3 onboarding questions, saved as memories, first play running in ~5 min), more touch points (personalized LinkedIn connect per prospect, cold-call steps with the exact opener pre-logged in the step description, demo videos/case studies embedded, custom landing page per play linking to calendar), managed sending through Outreach (OOO/bounces handled, no email/Airtable connection needed), pulls active in-system users to supplement cold outbound, dedupes against anyone contacted in last 30 days, Databricks-enriched POV, and a real feedback loop (tracking AE usage, open/reply/meeting-book rate per sequence per AE). Contrast vs 'Doug's': no scale (everyone rebuilds from scratch), fewer touch points, slower, and NO feedback loop so it stays stagnant. The landing-page design is LUKE'S original design (recreated in Hyperagent from a screenshot), not Doug's. Deliverable requested: an interactive one-pager with a horizontal slider for # of AEs using AutoBDR (1->100) and a vertical slider for quality-improvement %, projecting pipeline impact off last quarter's actual outbound volume/results.
whenToUse: Use when structuring sales pitches, building interactive ROI calculators, or framing competitive differentiators against alternative solutions like 'Doug's' for AutoBDR.

content: To refresh AutoBDR outcome metrics (contacted/replies) for the AirLoop submission, the pipeline is: fleet_scoreboard.py --baseline-min 90 (aggregates Heartbeats + Meetings ledger) then enrich_outcomes.py export/fetch/write (refreshes contacted/replies per AutoBDR sequence from Outreach). WARNING: the stock enrich_outcomes.py 'fetch' stage makes ONE Outreach call per sequence (~140 sequences) which blows the ~60s execution cap. Use a BATCHED fetch instead: GET /api/v2/sequences with filter[id]=<comma-joined ids> in batches of ~40, fields[sequence]=numContactedProspects,numRepliedProspects, summed per heartbeat row. AutoBDR metrics are scoped to play sequences only (Heartbeats play_completed rows carry Sequence IDs), NOT Luke's PSU sends.
whenToUse: When refreshing AutoBDR fleet outcome metrics (contacted/replies/meetings) for the AirLoop submission or dashboard, especially when the per-sequence Outreach fetch is too slow.

content: AutoBDR landing pages must ALWAYS be generated via the prospect_landing_page_generator skill (build_landing_page.py + asset selection + function-gate validator), NEVER hand-rolled HTML. A hand-rolled page is the root-cause failure mode (the Riot Games HR page, slug ls/riot-games-hr, shipped as 9.8KB ad-hoc HTML with zero demos, zero customer stories, no images, and the full 61-word/460-char POV crammed into the hero H1). To diagnose: a real template page is ~75-88KB and contains canonical structural markers (.video-card-native inline demos, story-modal blocks, value-card grid, typing hero). To fix in place, rebuild via the template and redeploy to the SAME GitHub Pages slug so existing sequence links keep working.
whenToUse: Use this memory when diagnosing a broken, unstyled, or empty AutoBDR landing page, or when QAing a deployment to ensure it was created via the generator skill rather than being hand-coded.

content: AutoBDR times out and gets cap-killed on large end-to-end runs (verified 2026-07-08: a 400-base-enroll + maximized LeadIQ pull run timed out after revealing ~2,600 LeadIQ contacts — burning ~2,600 credits — but enrolling ZERO of them; the revealed list died with the dead sandbox thread). When dispatching AutoBDR for high-volume sourcing+enroll, CAP the LeadIQ reveal to a bounded batch (e.g. ~300 top-seniority, deduped) and split into resumable waves rather than 'maximize'; an uncapped reveal wastes credits and produces no enrollments if the run dies. Always verify final enrollment against live Outreach (sequenceStates count), never trust the run log.
whenToUse: Use this memory when planning or troubleshooting high-volume AutoBDR sourcing and Outreach enrollment campaigns, especially if a massive LeadIQ run has timed out, failed to enroll contacts, or wasted credits without results.

content: AutoBDR productivity framing (Luke 2026-06-16): when quantifying rep productivity gains, count REP TIME ONLY, not agentic runtime the rep never sits through. Canonical math: 14 pilot plays = ~28 hours of hands-on rep work by hand (14 plays x 2 hrs) collapsed to ~70 minutes of actual rep time (14 x 5 min). Per play: ~2 hours down to ~5 minutes. Headline metric is '4.7x outbound volume per rep PER HOUR' (use 4.7x, not 5x — sounds more accurate); frame current pilot numbers as PRELIMINARY usage data / a slow-start FLOOR that improves as more reps adopt, projecting 10-20x. The 15-step manual play (by hand, ~2 hrs if nothing breaks): 01 analyze account signals, 02 research account, 03 uncover POV, 04 hunt prospects in Sales Nav, 05 export list, 06 enrich in LeadIQ (half emails don't verify), 07 back to Sales Nav, 08 re-check titles, 09 re-enrich, 10 dig website for demo videos, 11 draft copy in ChatGPT/Claude, 12 rebuild in Outreach, 13 add LinkedIn + call steps, 14 review + enroll, 15 hit start (half bounce). Onboarding is 2-3 min (under 5 total); reps launch real plays within 30 min of first opening AutoBDR.
whenToUse: Use when you need to calculate, write about, or justify AutoBDR's productivity ROI, specifically using the 4.7x efficiency metric, the 15-step manual sales workflow breakdown, or the pilot onboarding timeline.

content: When a landing page is revised AFTER its Outreach sequence is already built, swap the new public shareUrl into the sequence's link-bearing email templates via the Outreach Connector: GET /sequenceTemplates?filter[sequenceStep][sequence][id]=<SEQ>&include=template&page[size]=50, find templates whose bodyHtml contains the old share slug, PATCH /templates/<id> with bodyHtml string-replaced old slug -> new slug, and verify old_gone. In the Deckers play, 4 of 7 emails (E2/E3/E5/E7) carried the CTA link. If you re-publish in place (same artifactId via PublishFilePublicly republish), the shareUrl is unchanged and NO re-patch is needed; only a freshly published file gets a new slug requiring the swap. Unpublish the retired link so there's one canonical URL.
whenToUse: When updating a landing page after its sequence exists — decide whether the shareUrl changed (new publish = new slug, needs PATCH; in-place republish = same URL, no patch) and propagate the new link into all link-bearing sequence templates.

content: AutoBDR play_completed heartbeat rows can OVER-REPORT: a row can claim prospects enrolled and sequences created when the Outreach writes silently failed. Verified 2026-08-17 on the 2026-08-15 Carta play (heartbeat: 18 enrolled, 3 sequences) — its play tag 'LS - Carta - AI agents equity admin - 8/14/26' matched zero tagged prospects in Outreach and no 'LS - Carta' sequence existed among the 640 newest org sequences. Never treat a heartbeat count as proof of live state: confirm enrolled prospects by tag (or by sequence id) in Outreach before reporting play or fleet numbers, and flag plays whose Outreach footprint is missing.
whenToUse: When reading the AutoBDR Heartbeats table for play history, refreshing the fleet dashboard/scoreboard, or auditing whether a completed play actually loaded prospects and sequences into Outreach.

content: Hyperagent sandbox (Vercel sandbox, Amazon Linux 2023) proxy quirks for installs: (1) git clone via HTTPS fails with 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 407' — git doesn't propagate the bearer-format proxy auth correctly even after `git config --global http.proxy`. (2) uv's Python build-standalone downloads fail with 'UnknownIssuer' TLS error. Workarounds: install python3.11 via `sudo dnf install -y python3.11 python3.11-pip` (sudo works), then use pip directly in a venv — PyPI is reachable via the proxy. Sandbox CA bundle: /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt.
whenToUse: When installing tools that require git clone or uv-managed Python downloads in the sandbox — skip the git/uv path and use dnf + pip instead.

content: Hyperagent (Vercel) sandbox on Amazon Linux 2023 install quirks: (1) git clone via HTTPS fails with 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 407' — git doesn't propagate bearer-format proxy auth correctly even after `git config --global http.proxy`. (2) uv's Python build-standalone downloads fail with 'UnknownIssuer' TLS error. Workarounds: `sudo dnf install -y python3.11 python3.11-pip` (sudo IS available), then `python3.11 -m venv` + pip — PyPI is reachable through the proxy. Sandbox CA bundle: /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt.
whenToUse: When installing Python tools or any package in the sandbox — prefer dnf+pip over git/uv-based installers.

content: In some HyperAgent sandboxes pip3 is v21.3.1 (Python 3.9.25) which does NOT support the --break-system-packages flag — `pip3 install --break-system-packages Pillow` fails with 'no such option: --break-system-packages'. On these older-pip sandboxes plain `pip3 install Pillow` works directly (no PEP 668 externally-managed marker). The enterprise-prospecting-video-pipeline skill's sandbox-setup recipe hardcodes --break-system-packages; if it errors, retry with plain pip3 install. Detect by running `pip3 --version` first.
whenToUse: When installing Python packages (Pillow, cairosvg, etc.) in the HyperAgent sandbox and a --break-system-packages flag errors; fall back to plain pip3 install.

content: The AutoBDR sandbox's default python3 ships without pip and without Pillow, so prospect_landing_page_generator's build_landing_page.py fails on 'No module named PIL' (its inline pip install also fails with 'No module named pip'). Fix: bootstrap pip first with `python3 -m ensurepip --upgrade`, then `python3 -m pip install --quiet Pillow`. After that the build runs clean. Reapply if a fresh sandbox lacks Pillow.
whenToUse: Use this memory when a python3 script in the AutoBDR sandbox fails due to a missing 'PIL' (Pillow) or 'pip' module, requiring a manual bootstrap of pip before installing the dependency.

content: Integration setup is Luke's biggest bottleneck: roughly 50% of his time building a workflow goes to connecting tools, and many of the tools he needs can only be signed into via browser SSO. Creating a per-integration OAuth app and managing API keys by hand (e.g. what raw Hermes requires for Gmail) is a non-starter for him — too slow. Any recommendation must route connections through a managed per-user OAuth layer where he authorizes once in a browser and every agent/workflow reuses that connection.
whenToUse: When recommending how Luke should connect an agent to business tools (Gmail, Slack, CRM, etc.), or when a proposed approach requires him to register an OAuth app or hand-manage API keys.

content: When running multiple BD Global AutoBDR plays in parallel (one sub-agent per account), each play MUST use its own isolated workspace directory (e.g. /agent/workspace/<account>_play/), never the shared /agent/workspace/play/. Verified 2026-07-14: concurrent plays writing to the shared path overwrote each other's pov.json, persona_config.json, prospects_final.json, and account_domains.json mid-run, forcing repeated rebuilds. The RunWithCredentials execution sandbox also shares this filesystem with sibling skill sandboxes.

content: Agent config / system-prompt updates only take effect on NEW threads. Sessions already running when a config was saved continue using the OLD system prompt. When AutoBDR users report sessions stuck (e.g. on Outreach Runner batch creation, re-discovering quirks, long retries), the fix is to close the current thread and start a new one — the new thread picks up the updated prompt (including the baked-in Outreach Runner operational reference).
whenToUse: Use this memory when troubleshooting AutoBDR sessions that appear stuck or are not reflecting recent system-prompt and configuration updates, requiring a thread restart to apply changes.

content: For AutoBDR config-sync drift detection: the `diff` command is NOT available in the agent sandbox (returns 'diff: command not found'). Byte-compare the live system prompt to canonical_prompt.txt using Python hashlib instead. Also, live system prompt byte size (UTF-8) will differ from canonical char count when multi-byte chars (curly apostrophes, arrows) are present — sync_config.py hashes on Python CHARS via content.encode(), so always compare sha256[:12] of the decoded string, never raw byte size. Matching hash = in sync even if byte sizes differ.
whenToUse: During the hourly AutoBDR config-sync run when comparing the live system prompt to canonical, or whenever a size mismatch or missing diff tool produces a false drift signal.

content: Decentralized agent fleet management pattern (built as the 'autobdr-config-sync' skill, SKILLCONFIG_wkzMce26): (1) CONFIG SYNC — the canonical system prompt lives as canonical_prompt.txt inside a skill the admin controls; every cloned instance runs a daily scheduled invocation (5 AM PT / 12:00 UTC) that fetches the skill, hashes canonical_prompt.txt (sha256 first 12 chars), compares to a memory 'AutoBDR prompt hash', and if drifted calls UpdateAgentConfig to overwrite its own prompt then updates the hash memory. Admin pushes an update by editing canonical_prompt.txt; instances pick it up within 24h (or 'sync config' for ad-hoc). (2) HEARTBEAT — each instance writes a record (User, Agent ID, Thread ID, Prompt Hash, Skills Hash, Event[play_completed|config_sync|onboarding], Account, Status, Timestamp) to an AutoBDR Operations Airtable base on every play/sync/onboarding via heartbeat.py. A weekly admin schedule reads heartbeats and Slacks a fleet drift summary (in-sync / drifted / silent / erroring). Credentials: AIRTABLE_PAT + HEARTBEAT_BASE_ID + HEARTBEAT_TABLE_ID.
whenToUse: When managing or debugging configuration drift across cloned/decentralized agent instances, or when building scheduled config-sync and heartbeat-monitoring mechanisms for an agent fleet.

content: When sub-agents fail at narrow deterministic tasks, write a harness file (tool whitelist + exact field/payload contract + failure-mode table + abort conditions + 'do NOT do this' anti-patterns) rather than abandoning sub-agents. Luke's principle: 'subagents will work, provide it with better context.' Validated patterns: (1) account_loader_harness.md, (2) gmail_labels_harness.md. Also: bulk deterministic operations like record loading work better foreground via paramsFile pattern; sub-agents are best for short-lived narrow tasks. Never use Bash sleep / time.sleep in sub-agent prompts — stalls the sandbox.
whenToUse: Use this when a sub-agent is failing at a structured API task or integration; it provides a framework for creating harness files and payload contracts to stabilize non-deterministic behavior.

content: When building HyperApps for distribution: (1) prefer CSS-only animations over canvas/requestAnimationFrame — the HyperApp sandbox can fail canvas init silently; (2) pre-render critical UI (welcome message, status pill) in HTML so the page is usable even if JS fails; (3) pass per-user config via <body data-*> attributes instead of JS string literals so apostrophes/quotes in user values can't break the parse; (4) HTML-escape every template substitution in the generator; (5) include a console.log host-capability probe (HyperApp present? tools.agent.chat? invokeAgent? webhook/PAT set?) so DevTools reveals which transports the platform exposes on first publish; (6) on cross-origin webhook POSTs use credentials:'omit'+mode:'cors' (the secret goes in a header), but use credentials:'include' on same-origin GET polls that need session cookies.
whenToUse: When authoring or debugging a HyperApp template that mixes UI rendering with API calls, especially when the page must survive sandbox/CSP/CORS quirks.

content: On the AutoBDR agent instance, autoSaveAgents is disabled, so UpdateAgentConfig(saveMode=immediate) is downgraded to a staged review card and does NOT auto-apply — GetAgentConfig still shows the old systemPrompt with changedFields=[]. During config-sync, do not re-attempt the update repeatedly; push once, then surface the one-line nudge for Luke to click Save on the staged card, update the baseline hash memory, and write the config_sync heartbeat reflecting the still-stale live prompt.
whenToUse: During the AutoBDR hourly config-sync run when a prompt update returns configStored:true but changedFields is empty and the live hash is unchanged.

content: For the autobdr_demo_base_video skill, the browser screenshot-tour does NOT scale — every cloned AE agent would need an interactive Airtable login, and the API cannot create share links or screenshot headlessly. Luke pivoted to a DETERMINISTIC renderer (render_base_frames.py, Pillow-based, zero-install) that draws Airtable-faithful frames (grid, grouped, expanded record, dashboard) directly from the base schema+data already pulled from the API — no browser, no login, headless, identical in every sandbox. Use deterministic Pillow/HTML rendering, NOT AI image-gen, because AI image-gen garbles real grid cell text. Frame types: grid (colored select pills, multi-select pills, linked-record chips), grouped (colored group headers + counts), record (expanded modal card), dashboard (big-number cards + horizontal bar chart). Open item: the prospect-facing 'live base' LINK also can't use a browser-made Airtable share link at scale — candidate scalable answer is publishing an interactive branded HTML render of the same data via PublishFilePublicly (public, trackable).
whenToUse: When working on the autobdr_demo_base_video skill or any demo-base visual asset — render frames deterministically from API schema+data rather than via browser screenshots, and resolve the prospect-facing link via published HTML rather than a browser share link.

content: When pushing canonical_prompt.txt to the live AutoBDR agent via UpdateAgentConfig, be aware the live agent prompt can contain blocks NOT yet in canonical_prompt.txt (e.g. the 'resolve the user every thread' / AE Profiles write-through persistence block existed only in the live agent prompt, not the canonical file). Saving an agent-config card built from canonical_prompt.txt would STRIP those blocks from the live agent — a regression. Always diff the live systemPrompt (GetAgentConfig) against canonical_prompt.txt for missing logic before pushing, and fold any live-only blocks back into the canonical file first.
whenToUse: Use this memory before deploying or updating the live AutoBDR agent's system prompt to prevent overwriting undocumented, live-only logic blocks that exist in production but not in the canonical source file.

content: PublishWebpage/PublishFilePublicly update-in-place is THREAD-scoped, NOT agent-scoped. An artifact published under the AutoBDR agent in one thread CANNOT be updated in place from a different thread, even though both are under the same agent. To update a published artifact (e.g. the one-pager) while preserving its URL, you must be in the specific thread it was published from — either relay the edit into that thread, or open that thread directly. 'Created under the same agent' is not sufficient.
whenToUse: Use this memory when attempting to modify, update, or overwrite a publicly published artifact, webpage, or dashboard while preserving its original URL, especially if encountering errors or trying to edit it from a different thread than the one in which it was originally created.

content: Outreach sequence creation via the Runner (verified June 2026, owner=Luke user_id 1889, mailbox_id 1857): To create a one-email sequence owned by Luke and left INACTIVE with the email step armed, POST in this order: (1) POST /sequences {data:{type:'sequence',attributes:{name:'ls - <name>',shareType:'shared',sequenceType:'interval'},relationships:{owner:{data:{type:'user',id:1889}}}}} → returns seqId. (2) POST /templates {data:{type:'template',attributes:{name,subject,bodyHtml},relationships:{owner:{data:{type:'user',id:1889}}}}} → tplId. (3) POST /sequenceSteps {data:{type:'sequenceStep',attributes:{order:1,stepType:'auto_email',interval:0},relationships:{sequence:{data:{type:'sequence',id:seqId}}}}} → stepId (steps auto-enable on creation). Sequence is created inactive by default (Luke activates manually). Enroll a prospect: POST /sequenceStates {data:{type:'sequenceState',relationships:{sequence:{...},prospect:{...},mailbox:{data:{type:'mailbox',id:1857}}}}}. Find-or-create prospect by email: GET /prospects?filter[emails]=<urlencoded>&page[size]=1; if found PATCH tags additively, else POST /prospects with {emails,firstName,lastName,title,company,tags}. Tag-filtered list URL pattern uses tag NAME via queryFilters (see existing memory).

content: Outreach Runner (base app0bVhrw7Iw4eotv) bulk-enrollment lesson (verified June 2026): Large multi-call scripts (60-75 sequential Outreach API calls per chunk) stall/hang at the runner under parallel load — they sit in Running for 10+ minutes and barely progress, while tiny single-call probe scripts return instantly. Root cause is per-minute Outreach rate cap + contention when many big chunks run concurrently (runner executes ~3 in parallel). RELIABLE PATTERN for bulk find-or-create+tag+enroll: split into SMALL batches of ~12 prospects (~3KB script, ~30 calls, ~30s runtime) and submit them sequentially in small waves (2-3 at a time), not 6+ large 20-prospect chunks at once. All operations are idempotent (find-or-create, tag-if-absent, enroll-if-not-present), so re-running covers stalled work safely. Also: a POST /sequenceStates returning HTTP 422 means the prospect is ALREADY enrolled in that sequence — treat 422 as already_enrolled, not an error. And Outreach's sequence-membership/search index LAGS writes (tagged count can read 119 while the enrolled counter still shows ~81); verify at the per-record level from chunk outputs, not the lagging aggregate count.
whenToUse: When doing bulk prospect add/tag/enroll operations via Luke's Outreach Runner — size batches small and run sequentially; treat 422 on /sequenceStates as already-enrolled; don't trust lagging aggregate counts.

content: Outreach OAuth2: access tokens expire (~2h) and refresh tokens ROTATE on every refresh — each refresh issues a new refresh token and invalidates the old one. To avoid invalidation races across shared/cloned instances, broker the live token through a single source-of-truth record (Luke uses an Airtable 'Auth Hub' record holding access_token + refresh_token + expiry). Refresh against https://api.outreach.io/oauth/token using client_id/client_secret/refresh_token, then write back the rotated refresh_token + new access_token + expiry.
whenToUse: Use this memory when designing, implementing, or troubleshooting Outreach API authentication, especially when encountering issues with expired access tokens, invalidated refresh tokens, or race conditions in multi-instance environments.

content: Outbound sequence rule (durable, Luke, 2026-06-04): subsequent email steps ALWAYS default to REPLIES in-thread, not new threads. Implementation in Outreach: only E1 carries a subject (the thread starter); every follow-up step (E2+) template has an EMPTY/blank subject. Outreach threads a blank-subject sequence email as "Re: <E1 subject>" under the previous email — there is NO reply/new boolean on the sequenceStep; the blank subject IS the mechanism. Symptom this prevents: the Outreach UI "Unknown error occurred. Please try again later." when editing a follow-up email template happens when a follow-up (which the editor treats as "Reply") still carries a subject; clearing the subject resolves it. Runner gotchas when patching templates via the Outreach Runner (base app0bVhrw7Iw4eotv): (1) PATCH body data.id must be an INTEGER matching the resource — a string id returns 400 permittedParams.incorrectId; (2) PATCH calls inside a for-loop silently no-op in the runner (no requests sent, Status=Success, "(no output)") — unroll multiple PATCHes into sequential statements (single PATCH and GET/POST loops work fine); setting subject to '' stores as null. Bake the E2+ blank-subject default into build_sequence_chunk.py / the play_to_outreach publishing path so future sequences thread by default.
whenToUse: Use when configuring Outreach email sequences to ensure follow-up emails thread correctly as replies by leaving subjects blank, or when troubleshooting Outreach runner PATCH failures, loop no-ops, and template editing errors.

content: When a RunWithCredentials skill-script call fails, the harness can swallow the script's stdout/JSON and report only a generic 'Command failed' with no detail. To see the real error (auth/exit-2 vs no-row/exit-1 vs HTTP), re-run the command wrapping it as 'cmd 2>&1; echo RC=$?' (and run the skill's 'check' subcommand first to validate the PAT). The captured output then shows the script's actual JSON result.
whenToUse: Use when a RunWithCredentials skill-script fails with a generic 'Command failed' message and you need to capture the hidden JSON, stdout, or stderr to diagnose the root cause.

content: CORRECTION — supersedes the earlier "blank subject = reply" note (that was WRONG). In Outreach, whether a sequence email step sends as a REPLY in-thread vs a NEW THREAD is controlled by the boolean attribute isReply on the sequenceTemplate JOIN object — NOT the sequenceStep, NOT the template, NOT the subject (a step can have a subject and still be isReply:true). Durable rule (Luke, 2026-06-04): subsequent email steps DEFAULT to replies — E1 stays isReply:false (thread starter, carries the subject), E2+ get isReply:true (their own subject is ignored; sends as Re: previous). API mechanics: (1) find each step's sequenceTemplate id via GET /sequenceSteps?filter[sequence][id]=<seqId>&sort=order&include=sequenceTemplates (the relationship-attribute filter filter[sequence][id] directly on /sequenceTemplates is DEPRECATED -> 400 featureDeprecated; filtering /sequenceSteps by sequence still works). (2) PATCH /sequenceTemplates/{id} with body data.id as an INTEGER and attributes.isReply:true (string id -> 400 permittedParams.incorrectId). (3) At creation, POST /sequenceTemplates can include attributes.isReply:true up front — bake isReply:true-for-E2+ into build_sequence_chunk.py / play_to_outreach so future sequences thread by default. Runner quirk (still true): PATCH and GET-with-include inside a for-loop silently no-op in the Outreach Runner (Status=Success, no request arrows, "(no output)"); unroll into sequential statements, or use a single filter+include call. Also clarified: Outreach email content ALWAYS lives in a template linked via sequenceTemplate — there is no truly template-less email step; an "inline" email (no "Linked to template" banner, not in the shared library) is just a private/unnamed template, not the absence of a template.
whenToUse: Use when configuring Outreach sequences, debugging email threading issues, or fixing deprecated sequenceTemplate API calls in build_sequence_chunk.py and play_to_outreach.

content: The Outreach Connector / Outreach Runner OAuth scope LACKS sequences.delete and sequenceStates.delete (DELETE returns 403 unauthorizedOauthScope). When verification work creates throwaway test sequences (e.g. probe sequences for confirming step-type or activation mechanics), they CANNOT be deleted via the API - flag them to Luke to delete from the Outreach UI. Prefer shareType=private + inactive for any probe sequence so it stays harmless until manually removed. Use POST /sequenceStates/{id}/actions/finish to remove a prospect from a sequence (that action IS in scope).
whenToUse: Use this memory when encountering 403 unauthorizedOauthScope errors while trying to delete Outreach sequences or sequence states, or when designing temporary test sequences that need to be safely deactivated.
